reason: The cut must occur before the available clotting components can act; the rough edge is the visible cause.
expectation: The body will acquire a skin and vessel injury where bleeding can be stopped.

effect: The body now has a bleeding cut, with the vessel already narrowed; the clotting components can be used next.
reaction: The narrowed vessel is a useful initial detail.
reason: Platelets at the cut are the clearest next component for limiting the leak.
expectation: Platelets will collect at the damaged vessel and begin forming a plug.

effect: Platelets formed a plug that slows the leak; clotting factors and fibrinogen remain to reinforce it.
reaction: The distinction between slowing the leak and stopping it is useful.
reason: Activated clotting factors should convert soluble fibrinogen into the fibrin needed to strengthen the plug.
expectation: Fibrin will form and become available to reinforce the platelet plug.

effect: The clotting factors produced fibrin threads, which can now reinforce the platelet plug.
reaction: The thread mesh makes the reinforcement easy to picture.
reason: Fibrin threads and the platelet plug are the remaining complementary parts of a clot.
expectation: The fibrin mesh will stabilize the plug and stop the bleeding.

effect: The fibrin mesh stabilized the platelet plug and stopped the bleeding, while the skin remained open.
reaction: The distinction between sealing the vessel and healing the skin was useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Reinforcing the platelet plug with fibrin made the separate roles of platelets and the mesh clear, without implying the skin had already healed.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making fibrin threads was predictable, and its picture already placed the mesh among platelets before the final combination, making that separation slightly confusing.

surprise.text: The vessel was already narrowed when the cut appeared, before I used the platelets.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though making fibrin separately from the plug felt somewhat artificial because the picture showed threads forming among platelets.

continue.text: Yes. I would be interested to see how the still-open skin heals after bleeding stops; the chapter clearly leaves that process unresolved.
